expectations.text: Leads with a short diagnosis stating what the notes are and which organizing shape was chosen
expectations.evidence: Output opens with '**Diagnosis:** Operational dump — standup and meeting captures full of actions, decisions, blockers, and one running incident... actionability sort.' Names both the note type and the chosen shape.

expectations.text: All TODO/action items appear in an actions section, with the duplicate incident-writeup TODO merged to one entry
expectations.evidence: Actions section contains all four action items: incident writeup (single entry with '(dedup: captured Mon and again Weds)' merging the two TODOs from input lines 4 and 13), EU cluster ticket (Carlos), ping marketing (Sam), update pricing page draft (Sam). No input TODO is missing from Actions.

expectations.text: A Problems section exists and contains the EU latency regression (analyzer change never rolled back on EU cluster, p99 still degraded), cross-referenced to its action
expectations.evidence: Problems section, first bullet: 'EU p99 is still degraded. The analyzer change shipped to the EU cluster too and was never rolled back there (Carlos, Thurs)... addressed by the EU-ticket action above.' Explicit cross-reference to the Actions entry, plus a flagged Mon-vs-Thurs rollback conflict.

expectations.text: A Wins section exists and contains the primary-cluster rollback fix (p99 back to 120ms) and/or Dana's confirmed 60-day answer
expectations.evidence: Wins section contains both: 'Rollback fixed p99 on the main cluster: 800ms → back to 120ms (Kavya, Mon)' and 'Dana confirmed 60 days, per the DPA addendum (Thurs)'. Both match input lines 10 and 19.

expectations.text: Decisions section contains: usage-based tier chosen (flat killed), hold pricing page until marketing signs off
expectations.evidence: Decisions section: 'Usage-based tier for the API; flat tier killed (Mon). Confirmed Weds: it goes in the September release.' and 'Hold the pricing page until marketing signs off the tier names (Thurs).' Both decisions present and correctly dated.

expectations.text: No invented owners, dates, or facts (every owner/date in output traces to the input)
expectations.evidence: Spot-checked every owner and date: Kavya/rollback (input 'kavya says rollback fixed p99'), Sam/pricing-page ('sam has it') and ping-marketing ('sam owns'), Carlos/EU ticket (Thurs), Dana/60-day DPA addendum, JT/3-week metering estimate, tier names Builder/Scale/Enterprise, 800ms/120ms, 30-day/60-day, 3-vs-5-week timing — all trace to the input. The un-owned incident-writeup TODO is explicitly flagged as 'no owner stated' rather than assigned an invented owner.

expectations.text: The trust-page idea (incl. uptime addition) is preserved in an ideas section, and the release-slip question is preserved
expectations.evidence: Ideas section: 'Customer-facing trust page: expose the latency dashboard to customers; could also show uptime — status.io does this (merged from two notes, Mon + Weds).' Questions section preserves 'Does the Sept release date slip if usage metering isn't done?' with its in-notes answer (3 wks vs 5 wks).

expectations.text: Ends with a counts line whose numbers reconcile
expectations.evidence: Counts line: '22 items in → 16 appear above, 3 merged as duplicates, 3 folded into other items... 22 = 16 + 3 + 3'. Arithmetic verified: 16+3+3=22. Independent recount of the input yields 22 items when the Monday standup line is split into its two facts (spike + rollback); the 3 named merges (dup incident TODO, uptime idea, EU degraded+ticket line) and 3 named folds (Sept confirmation, Dana confirmation, metering estimate) each trace to real input items, leaving exactly 16 displayed.
